items.stem: What is the key difference between val and var in Scala?

options.text: A val binding cannot be reassigned, while a var can
options.rationale: Correct: val is an immutable binding; var allows reassignment.

options.text: A val is typed and a var is untyped
options.rationale: Both are statically typed; immutability is the distinction.

options.text: A val lives on the heap and a var on the stack
options.rationale: Memory placement is not what distinguishes them.

options.text: A val can only hold numbers
options.rationale: A val can hold any type.

items.explanation: Correct: val is an immutable binding; var allows reassignment.

items.stem: Which TWO are idiomatic ways to represent the possible absence or failure of a value in Scala?

options.rationale: Correct: Option models a value that may be absent.

options.text: Either, with Left for error and Right for success
options.rationale: Correct: Either carries either an error or a successful value.

options.text: Returning null when no value exists
options.rationale: null defeats the type system's absence handling and is discouraged.

options.text: Throwing an exception for every empty result
options.rationale: Routine absence is better modelled with Option than with exceptions.

options.text: Using a var set to -1 as a sentinel
options.rationale: Sentinel values are error-prone and non-idiomatic in Scala.

items.explanation: Correct: Option models a value that may be absent.

items.stem: When matching on a sealed trait, why does the compiler help you?

options.text: It can warn when the match does not cover all subtypes
options.rationale: Correct: a sealed trait has a known set of subtypes, so the compiler can check exhaustiveness.
Pattern matching is not parallelised by sealing a trait.

options.text: It converts the match into a database query
options.rationale: Matching has nothing to do with databases.

options.text: It makes the match run at compile time only
options.rationale: The match still executes at runtime.

items.explanation: Correct: a sealed trait has a known set of subtypes, so the compiler can check exhaustiveness.
